items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: people like Benny Carter, Duke Ellington, Art Tatum, I mean Fats Waller, Fletcher Henderson, Bix Beiderbecke.

ctx.x: So how did you get from that step to the actual playing? Was it through sheet music?

Yeah, and listening to records, mostly through listening to records. I used to try to play along with these Billie records and figure out what the tunes were. I always had a good ear for tunes and I’d try and find the chords around the tune. And it’s really — today’s world is very different. Because Duke Ellington was so prophetic when he said there will come a day when most jazz players will have to come out of a conservatory. And it’s all this training they’re getting now, you know, they’re going to these jazz…
Your bandmates today have said the same thing, almost verbatim. And they feel that most of the instructors that are teaching now grew up on Parker and Coltrane, so that’s where they feel —
